svg.text: Rank like ask, then go and read the source. The only verb that can say a citation is still true.
the refer plane -- fetched or retained bytes
1 - IT REUSES ASK'S PATH EXACTLY, WITH top = 3
Same gates, same tune, same scan-or-accelerator, same rank(), rerank, pin and graph tier, same band -- with top = 3 (constants.toml [answer] candidates, W-108).
answer takes ONE question and no -q (an RRF score would make the three incomparable), but --expand applies. Tier A, then Tier B, are handed to the refer plane; the band is Tier A's alone.
No results: a null answer, source "index", band none, and it stops. Since W-247 cmd_answer renders what build_answer computed, and fux.open().answer() reads the same builder.
2 - OBTAIN EACH OF THE THREE CANDIDATES, IN THIS ORDER
The decision ladder in _obtain() -- first match wins, and none of them can crash the query
Always, even when fetching is off. Reading your own checkout is not a fetch. A deleted file costs that one citation -- unverified, with a note naming it -- never the query.
Fetching is off for the whole repo (W-174): compare against .fux/acquired/, the bytes the record was built from. No fetcher is even loaded.
min(--cache-ttl, the URL line's own ttl=): a line can narrow the TTL and never widen it. External sources only; bounded by fux.toml [refer] fetch_cache_max_bytes.
fetch, bounded by fux.toml [refer] timeout_seconds (5 as shipped)
Your fetcher -- the one the line was ingested with, resolved per URL from .fux/sources/urls -- on one worker thread. A late result is dropped; the thread is abandoned, not joined.
The bytes are decoded by the line's decoder= exactly as ingest decoded them, sanitised, and only then hashed -- so the sha is comparable with the indexed one.
fetch failed -- raised, timed out, no fetcher, no decoder= line
Fall back to .fux/acquired/ (retained by default: [sources.url] keep = true); if that is empty too, say so rather than guessing.
A stale url: verdict is recorded to .fux/runtime/dirty so the next ingest refreshes that URL (W-82 §3.2). Fetchers are resolved per URL, not once: three candidates can sit behind three fetchers,
and verifying with the wrong one reports false staleness on every query. SR-CACHE's ARC content cache is not on this verb's path -- refer() is called with cache=None.
3 - THE FIVE VERDICTS, AND WHAT EACH ACTUALLY CLAIMS
we did not look at all
Only stale demotes the band (-> partial). cached and as-ingested do not -- and an as-ingested MISMATCH is an INDEX defect, not a stale source; its note says rebuild the record.
There is no max-age policy (W-58; SR-REFER decision 4). A record carries git's mtime, but nothing records when a citation was last verified, so an age bound would answer
"how old is this document" when the caller asked "how stale is my answer". Freshness is decided by content sha, which needs no clock.
4 - TURN THE BYTES INTO ONE CITED PASSAGE
file: bytes go through the same
The sha was taken on the RAW
bytes, one line earlier. url: text
passage. Tables band at 1 row per
A leading YAML block is passage
The SAME BM25F scorer, plus the
set's own df and n -- a fair
A passage is a two-field document:
is seated FIRST, so greedy score-
citation. All of it is [refer] in tune.
The locator is a line range: loc:L41-L58
Except for decoded documents -- a .docx's Markdown exists nowhere on disk, so a line number would be a confident lie. Those get loc#p3 with the heading beside it. --json carries ordinal either way.
5 - WHAT THE FLAGS CHANGE, AND WHAT EVERY CALL SAYS
Skip the fetch entirely. source becomes "index", the answer is the record's own title and headings, and verified stays "unverified" -- deliberately not upgraded.
[cli.answer] no_refer and [api] no_refer ship false, so refer is the default on every surface.
Per-document {freshness, indexed_sha, fetched_sha, strategy, note}, every citation, the byte budget used and dropped, and the policy the answer ran under.
An unsigned in-toto statement: index digest, tune digest, engine version and path, query and expansion, the band, the verdicts, the cited shas as subject. No wall clock.
fux verify checks it offline and never fetches: reproduced / drifted:corpus / drifted:config / unverifiable; --rerun re-answers the index path only.
The ONLY flag that writes. Appends the receipt to .fux/runtime/provenance.jsonl -- local, gitignored, kept to journal_max 1000; fux doctor warns above
journal_max_bytes, 4 MiB as shipped (W-246). [cli.answer] journal = true is the standing form of the same consent (L9).
Default 0 -- caching off. A caller who did not ask cannot be served a cached byte. Inert under fetch_at_answer = false, and it says so on stderr.
"nothing has changed since you last asked": the previous answer's (loc, sha) pairs in .fux/runtime/last-cited.json, compared and reported on stderr in text and
--json alike. A report, not a memo -- no answer is stored and nothing is replayed (SR-ANSWER decision 10). The band on stderr, the receipt digest, the audit summary: stderr too.
The one rule for every caller
A script that reads the answer and ignores the verdict field has thrown away the only thing separating fux from a stale cache with good manners.
NODE ANSWERS TOO, AND ITS VERDICT SET IS DELIBERATELY NARROWER
Node never fetches -- there is no transport in it and no seam to inject one. file: reads the working tree; url: reads .fux/acquired/ by the indexed sha if the blob was kept, else that
candidate is unverified; with no readable candidate at all the answer falls back to source: "index". The ranking in front of it is the same: top = 3, both tiers, --fast when the plane is fresh.
So current and stale are file:-only there, and cached can NEVER appear -- a TTL fetch cache requires fetching. as-ingested and unverified mean exactly what they mean here. --audit has a twin;
--receipt, --journal and --cache-ttl do not (W-107 R6). The frontmatter passage (W-254) is in the Node twin.
And Node has no decoder plane -- decode/registry.mjs knows only what is already text -- so rather than chunk the raw bytes of a document the index holds as decoded Markdown, it declines to refer it.
Drawn from the code, 2026-10-05. src/fux/query/__init__.py (build_answer), src/fux/query/refer_answer.py, src/fux/refer/*.py, src/fux/query/provenance.py, src/fux/constants.toml,
src/fux/templates/tune.toml.txt + output.toml.txt + fux.toml.txt, node/src/verbs/answer.mjs. SR-ANSWER - SR-REFER - SR-CACHE - SR-URL-FRESHNESS - SR-ACQUIRED - SR-PROVENANCE -
SR-CONFIDENCE - SR-NODE-SEARCH. The ranking in front of all this is architecture-ask.svg.
